subject: Acme: initial privacy engagement — DPA template & routing choice
body:
From: Sara Harris <sara.harris@acme-corp.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA request and data transfer routing question

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the intro call earlier. We’re preparing our privacy intake and would like to start with your standard DPA template. A few items we need clarified before we circulate internally:

- Do you support execution via DocuSign and AdobeSign? Procurement prefers DocuSign but I want to confirm it’s supported.
- We have EU-hosted data for EU customers. Will Redwood accept SCCs or is the default route binding corporate rules / other mechanisms?
- We use an SFTP vendor for log ingestion (third-party). Can you provide a subprocessors list or confirm whether that falls within your standard subprocessor disclosure?

If you can share your template and any guidance on transfer mechanisms (SCCs vs other), we’ll route to legal + procurement. Looking to get this completed before our renewal review on Dec 10.

Thanks,
Sara Harris
Senior Security & Privacy Ops
Acme Corp

---

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Sara Harris <sara.harris@acme-corp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA request and data transfer routing question

Sara — great to connect. Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up-front and attaching our current DPA template for review.

- E-sign: we support DocuSign as standard and can also accept AdobeSign if your legal team requires it. DocuSign is preferred for faster turnaround.
- Transfers: by default we offer SCCs (EU Standard Contractual Clauses) for EU transfers; for enterprise customers we also support derogations like SCCs + supplemental safeguards or custom Addenda depending on risk profile. If you need BCRs or something else, let us know and we’ll escalate to Legal.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a live subprocessor list; I’m attaching the standard DPA and will ask Legal to provide the latest subprocessor CSV or the vendor breakdown for SFTP ingest.

Attached: Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.2.docx

Next steps I propose: Laura (copied) can review any initial redlines and we can set a short cadence next week to walk procurement through the key clauses. Does Nov 24 at 10am PT work for a 30-min sync?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199

---

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Sara Harris <sara.harris@acme-corp.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:44:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: DPA request and data transfer routing question

Hi Sara,

Thanks for the prompt. I reviewed the template and made a few non-substantive clarifications and one suggested alternative for Section 6 (Data Transfers). I’m attaching a PDF with our comments and also included an optional clause that explicitly references SCCs + our supplemental administrative controls — this is typically acceptable to EU counsels.

On subprocessors: our standard practice is to provide a snapshot of subprocessors at contract signature, and we publish an up-to-date list on request. For SFTP/log vendors, please send the vendor domain or their vendor contact and I’ll confirm whether they are in scope.

I’m happy to join the Nov 24 sync; if procurement sends redline comments beforehand I can pre-flag negotiable items.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: ACME_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf

---

From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Harris <sara.harris@acme-corp.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:01:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA request and data transfer routing question

Thanks Laura/Jonas — attaching Acme’s initial redline. Main asks: tighten subprocessors notification window to 15 days, confirm audit rights language for SOC2 evidence, and prefer DocuSign. Also need to confirm whether logs sent to our SFTP partner (files@logs.acme-corp.com) are covered under the DPA or require a separate addendum.

Acme_Redline_v1.pdf attached.

Regards,
Tom Nguyen
Sr. Counsel, Procurement
Acme Corp

---

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-corp.com>, Sara Harris <sara.harris@acme-corp.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: DPA request and data transfer routing question

Tom/Sara — thanks for the redline and vendor detail. Quick status and plan: 

- Subprocessor notice window: we can accept 15 days for notification where feasible; for emergency security fixes we maintain the right to accelerate notices, but we’ll add an explicit carve (i.e., notification as soon as practicable for security incidents).
- Audit/SOC2: we cannot grant unrestricted on-site audits, but we can provide SOC 2 Type II reports on request and support a scoped audit for larger enterprise contracts. I’ve suggested language in our attached PDF.
- SFTP logs: after checking our subprocessor list, the logs partner you named is not currently engaged by Redwood. If you want them covered under the DPA, we can either: 1) add them to the subprocessor list once contract is executed and Redwood engages them, or 2) include an explicit assurance in the DPA that any third-party vendor we engage for log ingestion will be contractually bound by equivalent obligations. Option 2 is faster for your procurement review.

I’ll prepare a final DPA with the agreed changes and a DocuSign envelope. Expect a link by end of day Friday. If Nov 24 sync is still needed, I’m available for a shorter 20-min call; otherwise I’ll proceed with the DocuSign route.

Best,
Laura

---

Attachments referenced in thread:
- Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.2.docx (Redwood: standard DPA template)
- ACME_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf (Acme: initial redline)
